pages.x: After 711, Muslim armies conquered nearly all of Spain, which they called al-Andalus. Only in the mountains of the far north did Christians hold out. Around 722, tradition says, a noble named Pelayo beat a Muslim force at Covadonga and founded the kingdom of Asturias.

For three centuries al-Andalus was the richest land in western Europe. Córdoba, capital of the Umayyad caliphs of Spain, had paved and lit streets, hundreds of baths and a vast mosque, and Muslim, Jewish and Christian scholars worked there side by side.

When the caliphate broke up into small rival kingdoms in the 1000s, the Christian north pushed south, taking Toledo in 1085. The most famous warrior of the age, Rodrigo Díaz, El Cid, fought for Christian and Muslim rulers alike, and in 1094 took Valencia for himself.

Berber dynasties from Morocco, the Almoravids and then the Almohads, crossed over to fight back. But in 1212 the kings of Castile, Aragon and Navarre crushed the Almohads at Las Navas de Tolosa. Within 40 years Córdoba and Seville had fallen, and only Granada was left.

For 250 more years the kingdom of Granada survived, paying tribute to Castile. Its rulers built the Alhambra, a red-walled palace of courtyards, fountains and carved plaster, one of the masterpieces of Islamic art.

Isabella of Castile and Ferdinand of Aragon, whose marriage joined their kingdoms, fought ten years for Granada. On 2 January 1492 its last sultan, Muhammad XII, gave up the keys. Legend says he wept as he looked back, and his mother told him to weep like a woman for what he could not hold like a man.

Victory ended tolerance. In 1492 Spain's Jews were told to convert or leave, and tens of thousands went into exile. Muslims were forced to convert from 1502, and from 1609 their descendants, the Moriscos, were expelled too.

The Reconquista made Spain and Portugal crusading Catholic kingdoms, and in the very year it ended, Columbus sailed west. The mixing of cultures lives on in Spanish words such as aceite, oil, and in buildings from Córdoba to the Alhambra.
pts: Ended with the expulsion of Jews and Muslims
